title: 集合列与 σ 代数
summary: 定义集合列的上极限与下极限，并引入对补运算与可数并封闭的 σ 代数，为测度论确定「可测集合」的合法范围。
summaryEn: Limits of sequences of sets, and σ-algebras: families of sets closed under complements and countable unions, the legitimate universe of measurable sets in measure theory.
definition:
集合论里最基础的运算是并、交、补。给定全集 $X$（例如 $\mathbb{R}$），我们常常只关心一部分子集，希望它们在运算下「自给自足」。**集合列的上下极限**是极限概念的集合版本：设 $\{A_n\}_{n\ge1}$ 是 $X$ 的一列子集，称点 $x$ 属于**上极限** $\limsup_{n\to\infty}A_n$，如果 $x$ 属于无穷多个 $A_n$；称 $x$ 属于**下极限** $\liminf_{n\to\infty}A_n$，如果除有限多个 $n$ 外，$x$ 属于所有 $A_n$。用集合运算写出来就是 $$\limsup_{n\to\infty}A_n=\bigcap_{k\ge1}\bigcup_{n\ge k}A_n,\qquad \liminf_{n\to\infty}A_n=\bigcup_{k\ge1}\bigcap_{n\ge k}A_n.$$ 直观上，$\bigcup_{n\ge k}A_n$ 是「第 $k$ 项以后至少命中一次」的点，再对所有 $k$ 取交，就是「每一段尾巴都命中」，即无穷多次命中；对偶地，$\bigcap_{n\ge k}A_n$ 是「从第 $k$ 项起一直命中」的点，对所有 $k$ 取并就是「迟早一直命中」。显然恒有 $\liminf A_n\subseteq\limsup A_n$；当两者相等时，称集合列有极限 $\lim A_n$。

**$\sigma$ 代数**（读作 sigma 代数）是测度论中「可以测量的集合」的合法范围。$X$ 的子集族 $\mathcal{A}$ 称为 $\sigma$ 代数，如果 (1) $X\in\mathcal{A}$（含全集）；(2) $A\in\mathcal{A}\Rightarrow A^{c}=X\setminus A\in\mathcal{A}$（对补封闭）；(3) 若 $A_1,A_2,\dots\in\mathcal{A}$，则 $\bigcup_{n\ge1}A_n\in\mathcal{A}$（对**可数并**封闭）。注意第三条只要求可数并，不要求任意并。由德摩根律 $\left(\bigcup_n A_n\right)^{c}=\bigcap_n A_n^{c}$，对补封闭加上对可数并封闭立刻推出对**可数交**也封闭。由 (1)(2) 又得到 $\varnothing\in\mathcal{A}$，所以公理也可以等价地表述为：含全集、对补封闭、对可数并封闭。最简单的例子是 $\{\varnothing,X\}$ 与幂集 $2^X$，它们分别是「最粗」与「最细」的 $\sigma$ 代数，而它们中间的族才是有用的。

给定任意一个子集族 $\mathcal{E}$，包含 $\mathcal{E}$ 的所有 $\sigma$ 代数之交仍是 $\sigma$ 代数，称为由 $\mathcal{E}$ **生成**的 $\sigma$ 代数，记作 $\sigma(\mathcal{E})$——它是让 $\mathcal{E}$ 中每个集合都可测的「最省」的选择。实数轴上最重要的例子是由全体开集生成的 **Borel $\sigma$ 代数** $\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R})$。之所以先谈 $\sigma$ 代数：测度正是定义在它上面的集函数，只有先确定「哪些集合可测」，才谈得上「这个集合有多大」。
definitionEn:
Union, intersection and complement are the elementary operations on sets. Given a universal set $X$ (say $\mathbb{R}$), one usually singles out a family of subsets that is self-contained under these operations. **Limits of a sequence of sets** are the set-theoretic analogue of limits: for subsets $\{A_n\}_{n\ge1}$ of $X$, a point $x$ lies in the **limit superior** $\limsup_{n\to\infty}A_n$ if it belongs to infinitely many of the $A_n$, and in the **limit inferior** $\liminf_{n\to\infty}A_n$ if, apart from finitely many indices, it belongs to all of them. In set notation, $$\limsup_{n\to\infty}A_n=\bigcap_{k\ge1}\bigcup_{n\ge k}A_n,\qquad \liminf_{n\to\infty}A_n=\bigcup_{k\ge1}\bigcap_{n\ge k}A_n.$$ Intuitively $\bigcup_{n\ge k}A_n$ consists of the points that hit at least once after term $k$, and intersecting over all $k$ means hitting in every tail, i.e. infinitely often; dually, $\bigcap_{n\ge k}A_n$ consists of the points that stay in from term $k$ onwards, so the union over all $k$ means 'eventually always'. Always $\liminf A_n\subseteq\limsup A_n$; when the two coincide the sequence is said to have a limit $\lim A_n$.

A **$\sigma$-algebra** is the legitimate universe of 'measurable sets' in measure theory. A family $\mathcal{A}$ of subsets of $X$ is a $\sigma$-algebra if (1) $X\in\mathcal{A}$; (2) $A\in\mathcal{A}\Rightarrow A^{c}=X\setminus A\in\mathcal{A}$ (closed under complements); (3) $A_1,A_2,\dots\in\mathcal{A}\Rightarrow\bigcup_{n\ge1}A_n\in\mathcal{A}$ (closed under **countable unions**). Only countable unions are required, not arbitrary ones; by De Morgan's law $\left(\bigcup_n A_n\right)^{c}=\bigcap_n A_n^{c}$, closure under complements and countable unions yields closure under **countable intersections**. From (1) and (2) also $\varnothing\in\mathcal{A}$. The simplest examples are $\{\varnothing,X\}$ and the power set $2^X$, the coarsest and the finest $\sigma$-algebras on $X$.

For any family $\mathcal{E}$, the intersection of all $\sigma$-algebras containing $\mathcal{E}$ is again a $\sigma$-algebra; it is called the $\sigma$-algebra **generated** by $\mathcal{E}$ and written $\sigma(\mathcal{E})$ — the smallest choice making every set in $\mathcal{E}$ measurable. On the real line the key example is the **Borel $\sigma$-algebra** $\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R})$, generated by all open sets. $\sigma$-algebras come first because a measure is a set function defined on them: one must know which sets are measurable before asking how large they are.

formulas.note: 上极限：属于无穷多个 $A_n$ 的点全体，等价于对每个 $k$ 都在第 $k$ 项以后的并中出现。
formulas.noteEn: Limit superior: the set of points lying in infinitely many $A_n$, i.e. in the tail union for every $k$.

formulas.note: 下极限：至多漏掉有限多个 $A_n$ 的点全体（「最终一直命中」）。
formulas.noteEn: Limit inferior: points that miss at most finitely many of the $A_n$ ('eventually always in').

formulas.note: 下极限总包含在上极限里；两者相等时称集合列收敛，单调集合列必收敛。
formulas.noteEn: The inferior limit is always contained in the superior limit; equality defines convergence of the set sequence, which always holds for monotone sequences.

formulas.note: 德摩根律：配合对补封闭，σ 代数的可数并公理自动带来对可数交封闭。
formulas.noteEn: De Morgan's law: together with closure under complements, the countable union axiom yields closure under countable intersections.

formulas.note: σ 代数三条公理：含全集、对补封闭、对可数并封闭。
formulas.noteEn: The three axioms of a σ-algebra: contains $X$, closed under complements, closed under countable unions.

expression.text: limsup Aₙ = ∩_{k≥1} ∪_{n≥k} Aₙ，liminf Aₙ = ∪_{k≥1} ∩_{n≥k} Aₙ（「∪ 与 ∩ 交替」即可记忆）
expression.note: σ(ℰ) 是包含集合族 ℰ 的一切 σ 代数之交，也是让 ℰ 中集合全部可测的最小 σ 代数。
expression.noteEn: σ(ℰ) is the intersection of all σ-algebras containing ℰ, the smallest one in which every set of ℰ is measurable.

properties: 上极限由「属于无穷多个 $A_n$」刻画，下极限由「至多漏掉有限多个 $A_n$」刻画，且恒有 $\liminf A_n\subseteq\limsup A_n$。
σ 代数对补、可数并封闭，因而也对可数交、可数差封闭，并且必含 $\varnothing$ 与 $X$。
任意多个 σ 代数之交仍是 σ 代数，所以由集合族 $\mathcal{E}$ 生成的最小 σ 代数 $\sigma(\mathcal{E})$ 总存在；但两个 σ 代数之并一般不是 σ 代数。
有限 σ 代数恰由 $X$ 的某个有限划分生成，其元素个数为 $2^{k}$（$k$ 为划分的块数）。
单调集合列必收敛：$A_n\uparrow$ 时上下极限都等于 $\bigcup_n A_n$；$A_n\downarrow$ 时都等于 $\bigcap_n A_n$。
propertiesEn: The limit superior consists of the points in infinitely many $A_n$, the limit inferior of those missing at most finitely many; always $\liminf A_n\subseteq\limsup A_n$.
A σ-algebra is closed under complements and countable unions, hence also under countable intersections and countable differences, and contains both $\varnothing$ and $X$.

The intersection of any family of σ-algebras is again a σ-algebra, so the smallest σ-algebra $\sigma(\mathcal{E})$ generated by a family $\mathcal{E}$ always exists; a union of two σ-algebras usually is not a σ-algebra.
A finite σ-algebra is generated by a finite partition of $X$ and has exactly $2^{k}$ elements, where $k$ is the number of blocks.
Monotone sequences always converge: if $A_n\uparrow$ both limits equal $\bigcup_n A_n$, and if $A_n\downarrow$ both equal $\bigcap_n A_n$.

examples.problem: 设 $A_n=[0,2]$（$n$ 为偶数），$A_n=[1,3]$（$n$ 为奇数），求 $\limsup A_n$ 与 $\liminf A_n$。
examples.solution: $x\in\limsup A_n$ 当且仅当 $x$ 属于无穷多个 $A_n$。若 $x\in[0,2]$，则所有偶数项都含 $x$，故 $x\in\limsup A_n$；同理 $x\in[1,3]$ 时所有奇数项都含 $x$。反之若 $x\notin[0,3]$，则 $x$ 不属于任何 $A_n$。让两部分合起来得 $\limsup A_n=[0,3]$。而 $x\in\liminf A_n$ 要求从某一项起所有 $A_n$ 都含 $x$；从某项起既有偶数项也有奇数项，故 $x$ 必须同时属于 $[0,2]$ 与 $[1,3]$，即 $x\in[1,2]$；反之 $x\in[1,2]$ 时每个 $A_n$ 都含 $x$。因此 $\liminf A_n=[1,2]$，它严格包含于 $[0,3]$。

逐条验证公理。含全集：$\{1,2,3\}\in\mathcal{A}$。对补封闭：$\{1\}^{c}=\{2,3\}$、$\{2,3\}^{c}=\{1\}$、$\varnothing^{c}=X$ 都仍在 $\mathcal{A}$ 中。对有限并封闭（有限族只需验证有限并）：$\{1\}\cup\{2,3\}=X$，与 $\varnothing$ 或 $X$ 的并仍是自身或 $X$，故封闭。所以 $\mathcal{A}$ 是 σ 代数，它就是由划分 $\{\{1\},\{2,3\}\}$ 生成的 σ 代数。对照：$\mathcal{A}'=\{\varnothing,\{1\},\{2\},X\}$ 不是 σ 代数，因为 $\{1\}\cup\{2\}=\{1,2\}\notin\mathcal{A}'$。

title: 勒贝格外测度
summary: 用可数多个开区间的长度总和从外部覆盖任意集合，取下确界便得到对一切子集都有定义的勒贝格外测度。
summaryEn: Covering an arbitrary set from outside by countably many open intervals and taking the infimum of the total lengths gives the Lebesgue outer measure, defined for every subset of the line.
definition:
对任意集合 $E\subseteq\mathbb{R}$，我们想给它一个「长度」。直接沿用几何直觉对一般集合无从下手，但任何集合总可以被可数多个开区间盖住；这些区间的长度总和提供了 $E$ 大小的一个上界，而这个上界越小就越贴近真正的长度。

**定义**：$E\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ 的**勒贝格外测度**为 $$m^{*}(E)=\inf\Bigl\{\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}|I_k| : E\subseteq\bigcup_{k=1}^{\infty}I_k\Bigr\},$$ 这里的 $I_k$ 取遍开区间，$|I_k|$ 表示其长度（有限区间 $I=(a,b)$ 时 $|I|=b-a$，空区间长为 $0$）。有限个区间的覆盖只要补上若干个空区间就变成可数覆盖，所以「可数覆盖」已包含「有限覆盖」的情形；又因为每个 $E$ 都有覆盖（例如用 $\mathbb{R}$ 自身），下确界总是对非空集合取的，取值于 $[0,+\infty]$。

这个定义抓住了「用简单形状从外面逼近」的思想，由此立刻得到一串性质：非负性 $m^{*}(E)\ge0$；**单调性** $E\subseteq F\Rightarrow m^{*}(E)\le m^{*}(F)$（覆盖 $F$ 的区间族当然也覆盖 $E$，下确界只会更小）；平移不变性 $m^{*}(E+t)=m^{*}(E)$；以及最关键的**可数次可加性** $$m^{*}\Bigl(\bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty}E_n\Bigr)\le\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}m^{*}(E_n).$$ 证明的思路是把每个 $E_n$ 的覆盖拼起来、再用 $2^{-n}\varepsilon$ 控制总长度。注意这里只有单侧不等式，因为「从外面盖」天然只能给上界。

必须强调：外测度**一般不是可加的**。取区间内一个维塔利集 $E$，则 $E$ 与它的补集 $[0,1]\setminus E$ 不交，却有 $m^{*}(E)+m^{*}([0,1]\setminus E)>1=m^{*}([0,1])$，即 $m^{*}(E_1\cup E_2)<m^{*}(E_1)+m^{*}(E_2)$。修补这一缺陷正是引入**可测集**的动机：把满足卡拉西奥多里条件的集合挑出来，外测度限制在它们身上才是真正的测度。所以可以说，外测度是打补丁的工具，可测集才是正式的测度。
definitionEn:
For an arbitrary set $E\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ we want to assign a 'length'. Geometric intuition does not tell us what to do for a general set, but any set can be covered by countably many open intervals; the sum of their lengths is an upper bound for the size of $E$, and the smaller this bound the closer we are to the true length.

**Definition.** The **Lebesgue outer measure** of $E\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ is $$m^{*}(E)=\inf\Bigl\{\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}|I_k| : E\subseteq\bigcup_{k=1}^{\infty}I_k,\ I_k\ \text{open intervals}\Bigr\},$$ where $|I_k|$ is the length of $I_k$ ($|I|=b-a$ for $I=(a,b)$, and $0$ for an empty interval). A finite cover becomes a countable one by adding empty intervals, so the infimum is taken over a nonempty family for every $E$, and the values lie in $[0,+\infty]$.

The construction captures approximation from outside by simple shapes, and it immediately yields: nonnegativity $m^{*}\ge0$; **monotonicity** $E\subseteq F\Rightarrow m^{*}(E)\le m^{*}(F)$, since a cover of $F$ also covers $E$; translation invariance $m^{*}(E+t)=m^{*}(E)$; and most importantly **countable subadditivity** $$m^{*}\Bigl(\bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty}E_n\Bigr)\le\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}m^{*}(E_n),$$ proved by pasting together covers of the single sets and controlling the total length by an $2^{-n}\varepsilon$ argument. Only one-sided inequalities appear here, because covering from outside can only produce upper bounds.

It must be stressed that outer measure is **not additive in general**. Take a Vitali set $E$ inside $[0,1]$; then $E$ and its complement are disjoint and yet $m^{*}(E)+m^{*}([0,1]\setminus E)>1=m^{*}([0,1])$, i.e. $m^{*}(E_1\cup E_2)<m^{*}(E_1)+m^{*}(E_2)$ for disjoint sets. Repairing this defect is precisely the motivation for **measurable sets**: one singles out the sets satisfying Carathéodory's condition, and on them the outer measure becomes a genuine measure. Thus the outer measure is the patch, while the measurable sets are the real thing.

formulas.note: 定义：所有可数开区间覆盖的长度和的下确界；把开区间换成闭区间或半开区间得到的值相同。
formulas.noteEn: Definition: the infimum of the total lengths of all countable covers by open intervals; using closed or half-open intervals gives the same value.

formulas.note: 非负性与单调性：覆盖 $F$ 的区间族同样覆盖 $E$。
formulas.noteEn: Nonnegativity and monotonicity: any cover of $F$ also covers $E$.

formulas.note: 可数次可加性：不要求 $E_n$ 两两不交，这是外测度最常用的性质。
formulas.noteEn: Countable subadditivity: no disjointness is required; this is the most used property of outer measure.

formulas.note: 区间的外测度就是长度；外测度在平移下不变。可数集的（外）测度为 $0$，例如稠密的 $\mathbb{Q}$。
formulas.noteEn: An interval has outer measure equal to its length, and the outer measure is translation invariant. Countable sets such as the dense $\mathbb{Q}$ have outer measure 0.

formulas.note: 一般不可加：存在不交集合使次可加性取严格不等号，这正是引入可测集的原因。
formulas.noteEn: Not additive in general: disjoint sets can violate additivity strictly, which motivates measurable sets.

expression.text: m*(E) = inf { Σₖ|Iₖ| : E ⊆ ∪ₖ Iₖ，Iₖ 为开区间 }
expression.note: 外测度对每个 E ⊆ ℝ 都有定义，但一般不满足可加性，「长度」的正式版本要等到可测集。
expression.noteEn: The outer measure is defined for every subset of ℝ, but is not additive in general; the official version of 'length' waits for measurable sets.

properties: 外测度对 $\mathbb{R}$ 的每个子集（包括病态集合）都有定义，取值在 $[0,+\infty]$ 内。
非负且单调：$E\subseteq F\Rightarrow m^{*}(E)\le m^{*}(F)$，并且 $m^{*}(\varnothing)=0$。
可数次可加：$m^{*}(\bigcup_n E_n)\le\sum_n m^{*}(E_n)$，不需要 $E_n$ 两两不交。
平移不变，且 $m^{*}([a,b])=b-a$；可数集的（外）测度为 $0$，尽管它可以很稠密（如 $\mathbb{Q}$）。
一般不可加：存在不交集合 $E_1,E_2$ 使 $m^{*}(E_1\cup E_2)<m^{*}(E_1)+m^{*}(E_2)$，这是可测集概念出场的原因。
propertiesEn: Defined for every subset of $\mathbb{R}$, pathological ones included, with values in $[0,+\infty]$.
Nonnegative and monotone: $E\subseteq F$ implies $m^{*}(E)\le m^{*}(F)$, and $m^{*}(\varnothing)=0$.
Countably subadditive: $m^{*}(\bigcup_n E_n)\le\sum_n m^{*}(E_n)$, with no disjointness assumption.
Translation invariant, with $m^{*}([a,b])=b-a$; countable sets (such as the dense set $\mathbb{Q}$) have outer measure 0.
Not additive in general: there are disjoint $E_1,E_2$ with $m^{*}(E_1\cup E_2)<m^{*}(E_1)+m^{*}(E_2)$, which brings measurable sets onto the stage.

examples.problem: 证明任意可数集 $E=\{x_1,x_2,\dots\}\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ 的外测度为 $0$。
examples.solution: 任取 $\varepsilon>0$。对每个 $k$ 取开区间 $I_k=\left(x_k-\frac{\varepsilon}{2^{k+1}},\ x_k+\frac{\varepsilon}{2^{k+1}}\right)$，则 $|I_k|=\frac{\varepsilon}{2^{k}}$，且 $E\subseteq\bigcup_{k\ge1}I_k$。由定义 $$m^{*}(E)\le\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}|I_k|=\varepsilon\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}2^{-k}=\varepsilon.$$ 由于 $\varepsilon>0$ 任意，$m^{*}(E)\le\inf_{\varepsilon>0}\varepsilon=0$；又外测度非负，故 $m^{*}(E)=0$。特别地 $m^{*}(\mathbb{Q})=0$：有理数虽然稠密，总长度却是零。

上界：对任意 $\varepsilon>0$，$[0,1]\subseteq(-\varepsilon,1+\varepsilon)$，故 $m^{*}([0,1])\le1+2\varepsilon$，令 $\varepsilon\to0^{+}$ 得 $m^{*}([0,1])\le1$。下界：设 $[0,1]\subseteq\bigcup_{k=1}^{\infty}I_k$ 是任一可数开区间覆盖。由海涅-博雷尔有限覆盖定理，存在有限子覆盖 $I_{k_1},\dots,I_{k_N}$，而有限多个区间的并的长度不超过长度之和（用归纳法即可证明），因此 $$\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}|I_k|\ge\sum_{j=1}^{N}|I_{k_j}|\ge\Bigl|\bigcup_{j=1}^{N}I_{k_j}\Bigr|\ge1.$$ 于是任何覆盖的长度和都 $\ge1$，取下确界得 $m^{*}([0,1])\ge1$。两方向合起来 $m^{*}([0,1])=1$。

title: 可测集与勒贝格测度
summary: 满足卡拉西奥多里条件的集合称为可测集；它们构成 σ 代数，外测度限制在其上便是可数可加且完备的勒贝格测度。
summaryEn: Sets satisfying the Carathéodory condition are called measurable; they form a σ-algebra, and the outer measure restricted to them is the countably additive and complete Lebesgue measure.
definition:
外测度对一切集合都有定义，但一般不可加。为了让「长度」变成真正好用的测度，卡拉西奥多里给出了一个巧妙的判据：**把所有集合都当作「尺子」来检验**。集合 $E\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ 称为**可测的**，如果对**任意** $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ 都有 $$m^{*}(A)=m^{*}(A\cap E)+m^{*}(A\cap E^{c}).$$ 注意 $A$ 是任意的「测试集」，只验证 $A=\mathbb{R}$ 这一个情形是不够的；又由次可加性 $m^{*}(A)\le m^{*}(A\cap E)+m^{*}(A\cap E^{c})$ 自动成立，所以实际只需验证 $\ge$ 方向。

这个条件的意义是：$E$ 能把任何集合 $A$ 干净利落地「切开」，两侧的外测度相加而不漏水。可以证明，满足条件的集合类 $\mathcal{M}$ 构成一个 σ 代数：$\varnothing,\mathbb{R}\in\mathcal{M}$；条件本身关于 $E$ 与 $E^{c}$ 对称，故对补封闭；并且对可数并封闭。于是把 $m^{*}$ 限制在 $\mathcal{M}$ 上，记 $m=m^{*}|_{\mathcal{M}}$，就得到**勒贝格测度**，它满足 σ 可加性：对 $\mathcal{M}$ 中两两不交的集合列 $\{E_n\}$，$$m\Bigl(\bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty}E_n\Bigr)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}m(E_n).$$

哪些集合可测？开区间可测，从而一切开集、闭集以及它们的可数并、交、补（即一切 Borel 集）都可测；特别地所有区间都可测，且 $m([a,b])=b-a$。此外勒贝格测度是**完备的**：若 $m(N)=0$，则 $N$ 的任何子集也可测且测度为 $0$——这是黎曼积分理论无法提供的性质，它让「忽略零测集」成为合法的操作。

康托尔集是最著名的例子：从 $[0,1]$ 出发，每一步把每个剩余区间中间的 $1/3$ 开区间挖去。剩下的集合 $C$ 不可数，但挖去的总长度为 $\frac13+\frac29+\frac4{27}+\cdots=1$，所以 $m(C)=0$。它说明「不可数」推不出「测度为正」，也说明实数轴上有大量「看不见」的零测集。可测集类把这些病态集合隔离出来，使分析可以在干净的舞台上进行。
definitionEn:
Outer measure is defined for every set but is not additive. To turn 'length' into a genuinely useful measure, Carathéodory found a clever test: use **all** sets as rulers. A set $E\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ is called **measurable** if for **every** $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, $$m^{*}(A)=m^{*}(A\cap E)+m^{*}(A\cap E^{c}).$$ The test set $A$ is arbitrary — checking only $A=\mathbb{R}$ is not enough — and by subadditivity the inequality $\le$ is automatic, so only the direction $\ge$ has to be verified.

The condition means that $E$ cuts every set $A$ cleanly into two parts whose outer measures add up with no loss. One proves that the class $\mathcal{M}$ of measurable sets is a σ-algebra: $\varnothing,\mathbb{R}\in\mathcal{M}$; the condition is symmetric in $E$ and $E^{c}$, so $\mathcal{M}$ is closed under complements; and it is closed under countable unions. Restricting $m^{*}$ to $\mathcal{M}$, written $m=m^{*}|_{\mathcal{M}}$, gives **Lebesgue measure**, which is countably additive: for pairwise disjoint $E_n\in\mathcal{M}$, $$m\Bigl(\bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty}E_n\Bigr)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}m(E_n).$$

Which sets are measurable? Every open interval is; hence so are all open sets, closed sets, and their countable unions, intersections and complements — i.e. all Borel sets. In particular every interval is measurable with $m([a,b])=b-a$. Moreover Lebesgue measure is **complete**: if $m(N)=0$ then every subset of $N$ is measurable with measure $0$, a feature the Riemann theory cannot offer, and the legal basis for ignoring null sets.

The Cantor set is the standard example: starting from $[0,1]$, remove at each step the open middle third of every remaining interval. The remainder $C$ is uncountable, yet the total length removed is $\frac13+\frac29+\frac4{27}+\cdots=1$, so $m(C)=0$. Thus 'uncountable' does not imply 'positive measure', and there are plenty of invisible null sets on the line. The measurable sets isolate the pathologies and provide a clean stage for analysis.

formulas.note: 卡拉西奥多里条件：对任意测试集 $A$ 成立；结合次可加性只需验证 $\ge$ 方向。不能只对 $A=\mathbb{R}$ 验证。
formulas.noteEn: Carathéodory's condition: it must hold for every test set $A$; by subadditivity only the inequality $\ge$ needs checking, and $A=\mathbb{R}$ alone is insufficient.

formulas.note: 勒贝格测度的 σ 可加性：这是它成为「测度」的核心性质，有限可加是其特例。
formulas.noteEn: Countable additivity of Lebesgue measure, the core property making it a measure; finite additivity is a special case.

formulas.note: 完备性：零测集的任何子集仍可测且零测。
formulas.noteEn: Completeness: every subset of a null set is measurable and null.

formulas.note: 区间的勒贝格测度等于其长度（开闭不限）。
formulas.noteEn: The measure of an interval equals its length, open or closed alike.

formulas.note: 康托尔集：挖去的总长度为 $1$，剩下不可数的零测集。
formulas.noteEn: The Cantor set: the removed pieces have total length 1, leaving an uncountable null set.

expression.text: E 可测 ⟺ 对任意 A ⊆ ℝ：m*(A) = m*(A∩E) + m*(A∩Eᶜ)
expression.note: 卡拉西奥多里条件中的 A 可以是任何集合，包括病态集合；这正是「可测」一词的精确含义。
expression.noteEn: The test set A in Carathéodory's condition may be any set, including pathological ones; this is the precise meaning of 'measurable'.

properties: 可测集类 $\mathcal{M}$ 是 σ 代数，包含所有开集、闭集与区间，因此一切 Borel 集都可测。
勒贝格测度在 $\mathcal{M}$ 上可数可加，且 $m(\varnothing)=0$；单调性与有限可加性是它的推论。
$m$ 是完备的：若 $m(E)=0$，则 $E$ 的任何子集都可测且测度为 $0$。
平移不变：$E\in\mathcal{M}\iff E+t\in\mathcal{M}$，且 $m(E+t)=m(E)$。
区间测度等于长度，可数集零测；但不可数集也可以零测（康托尔集），所以「不可数 $\Rightarrow$ 测度为正」是错的。
propertiesEn: The measurable sets form a σ-algebra containing all open sets, closed sets and intervals; hence every Borel set is measurable.
Lebesgue measure is countably additive on $\mathcal{M}$ with $m(\varnothing)=0$; monotonicity and finite additivity follow.
$m$ is complete: every subset of a set of measure zero is measurable and has measure zero.
Translation invariance: $E$ is measurable iff $E+t$ is, and $m(E+t)=m(E)$.
Intervals get their length and countable sets are null, yet an uncountable set can also be null (the Cantor set), so uncountability does not force positive measure.

examples.problem: 从 $[0,1]$ 出发，每一步把每个剩余区间中间的 $1/3$ 开区间挖去，得到康托尔集 $C$。求 $m(C)$，并说明 $C$ 不可数。
examples.solution: 第 $k$ 步挖去的开区间共有 $2^{k-1}$ 个，每个长为 $3^{-k}$，故挖去的总长度为 $$\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}2^{k-1}3^{-k}=\frac13\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\Bigl(\frac23\Bigr)^{k-1}=\frac{1/3}{1-2/3}=1.$$ 挖去的集合是可数个开区间之并，可测；因此 $$m(C)=m([0,1])-1=1-1=0.$$ 不可数性：$C$ 中的点都可以写成只含数字 $0$ 与 $2$ 的三进制小数；把这种展开中的每个 $2$ 换成 $1$，就得到一串 $0$-$1$ 序列，而每个二进制展开都以这种方式出现，于是从 $C$ 到 $[0,1]$ 存在满射；又 $C\subseteq[0,1]$，故 $C$ 与 $[0,1]$ 等势，特别地不可数。结论：不可数集的勒贝格测度可以为 $0$。

examples.problem: 证明：若 $m^{*}(E)=0$，则 $E$ 可测（即任何零测集的子集都可测，这解释了勒贝格测度的完备性）。
examples.solution: 对任意 $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$：由单调性 $m^{*}(A\cap E)\le m^{*}(E)=0$，故 $m^{*}(A\cap E)=0$；又 $m^{*}(A\cap E^{c})\le m^{*}(A)$。另一方面 $A\subseteq(A\cap E)\cup(A\cap E^{c})$，由次可加性 $$m^{*}(A)\le m^{*}(A\cap E)+m^{*}(A\cap E^{c})=m^{*}(A\cap E^{c})\le m^{*}(A).$$ 于是等号成立，即 $m^{*}(A)=m^{*}(A\cap E)+m^{*}(A\cap E^{c})$，卡拉西奥多里条件满足，$E$ 可测且 $m(E)=0$。注意这里 $E$ 事先不必可测，只要外测度为 $0$。

title: 测度空间与测度的性质
titleEn: Measure Spaces and Properties of Measures
summary: 在 σ 代数上定义非负、可数可加的集函数即测度，三元组 (X, ℱ, μ) 称为测度空间；测度具有单调性、次可加性与连续性。
summaryEn: A measure is a nonnegative countably additive set function on a σ-algebra; the triple (X, ℱ, μ) is a measure space, and measures enjoy monotonicity, subadditivity and continuity.
definition:
σ 代数确定了「可以测量的集合」，接下来给这些集合赋「大小」。设 $X$ 是非空集合，$\mathcal{F}$ 是 $X$ 上的 σ 代数。**测度**是函数 $\mu:\mathcal{F}\to[0,+\infty]$，满足：(i) $\mu(\varnothing)=0$；(ii) **可数可加性**：若 $A_1,A_2,\dots\in\mathcal{F}$ 两两不交，则 $$\mu\Bigl(\bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty}A_n\Bigr)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\mu(A_n).$$ 三元组 $(X,\mathcal{F},\mu)$ 称为**测度空间**，$\mathcal{F}$ 中的集合称为**可测集**。非负性与 $\mu(\varnothing)=0$ 让测度像「长度」「面积」「概率」一样自然。

从可数可加性出发，可以推出一整套常用性质：**单调性** $A\subseteq B\Rightarrow\mu(A)\le\mu(B)$（且当 $\mu(A)<\infty$ 时 $\mu(B\setminus A)=\mu(B)-\mu(A)$）；**可数次可加性** $\mu(\bigcup_n A_n)\le\sum_n \mu(A_n)$（不要求不交）；以及**上下连续性**：若 $\{A_n\}$ 递增（$A_n\subseteq A_{n+1}$），则 $$\mu\Bigl(\bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty}A_n\Bigr)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\mu(A_n);$$ 若 $\{A_n\}$ 递减，则**必须附加条件 $\mu(A_1)<\infty$**，才有 $$\mu\Bigl(\bigcap_{n=1}^{\infty}A_n\Bigr)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\mu(A_n).$$ 这个条件不能省：在 $\mathbb{R}$ 上取勒贝格测度与 $A_n=[n,\infty)$，交集为 $\varnothing$、测度为 $0$，而 $\lim m(A_n)=+\infty$，等式失效的根源正是 $m(A_1)=\infty$。

概率论是测度论的特例：概率空间 $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},P)$ 就是满足 $P(\Omega)=1$ 的测度空间，「事件」是 $\mathcal{F}$ 中的集合，「事件的概率」是 $\mu$；计数测度 $\mu(A)=|A|$ 则给出另一类离散模型。若 $\mu(X)<\infty$ 称 $\mu$ 为**有限测度**；若 $X$ 可被可数多个有限测度集覆盖，称 $\mu$ 为 **σ 有限**。勒贝格测度不是有限测度，但它在每个区间上有限，所以是 σ 有限的。

抽象测度空间的价值在于「一次证明、多处使用」：勒贝格积分、概率、计数测度共享同一套推理，后面所有的积分与收敛定理都只需在任意测度空间中证明一遍。
definitionEn:
A σ-algebra tells us which sets may be measured; a measure tells us how big they are. Let $X$ be a nonempty set and $\mathcal{F}$ a σ-algebra on $X$. A **measure** is a function $\mu:\mathcal{F}\to[0,+\infty]$ such that (i) $\mu(\varnothing)=0$; (ii) **countable additivity**: for pairwise disjoint $A_1,A_2,\dots\in\mathcal{F}$, $$\mu\Bigl(\bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty}A_n\Bigr)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\mu(A_n).$$ The triple $(X,\mathcal{F},\mu)$ is a **measure space** and the members of $\mathcal{F}$ are the **measurable sets**. Nonnegativity and $\mu(\varnothing)=0$ make $\mu$ behave like length, area or probability.

From countable additivity one derives the working properties: **monotonicity** $A\subseteq B\Rightarrow\mu(A)\le\mu(B)$ (and $\mu(B\setminus A)=\mu(B)-\mu(A)$ when $\mu(A)<\infty$); **countable subadditivity** $\mu(\bigcup_n A_n)\le\sum_n\mu(A_n)$ with no disjointness needed; and **continuity**: for an increasing sequence $A_n\uparrow A$, $$\mu(A)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\mu(A_n),$$ while for a decreasing sequence $A_n\downarrow A$ one needs the extra hypothesis $\mu(A_1)<\infty$ to conclude the same. The hypothesis cannot be dropped: with Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}$ and $A_n=[n,\infty)$, the intersection is empty of measure $0$ while $\lim m(A_n)=+\infty$, precisely because $m(A_1)=\infty$.

Probability theory is a special case: a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},P)$ is a measure space with $P(\Omega)=1$, events are the sets of $\mathcal{F}$, and counting measure $\mu(A)=|A|$ gives a discrete model. A measure is **finite** if $\mu(X)<\infty$, and **σ-finite** if $X$ can be covered by countably many sets of finite measure. Lebesgue measure is not finite but is σ-finite, being finite on every interval.

The value of the abstract setting is 'prove once, use everywhere': Lebesgue integration, probability and counting share one body of reasoning, and all later integration and convergence theorems are proved once in an arbitrary measure space.

formulas.note: 可数可加性：测度公理的核心，要求集列两两不交。
formulas.noteEn: Countable additivity, the heart of the axioms, required for pairwise disjoint sets.

formulas.note: 单调性；若再假设 $\mu(A)<\infty$，则 $\mu(B\setminus A)=\mu(B)-\mu(A)$，有限性条件不可省。
formulas.noteEn: Monotonicity; if moreover $\mu(A)<\infty$, then $\mu(B\setminus A)=\mu(B)-\mu(A)$, and the finiteness hypothesis cannot be dropped.

formulas.note: 可数次可加性：不要求集列不交，是最常用的估计工具。
formulas.noteEn: Countable subadditivity, valid without disjointness and the most used estimate.

formulas.note: 递增连续性（下连续），不需要任何有限性假设。
formulas.noteEn: Continuity from below for increasing sequences, requiring no finiteness assumption.

formulas.note: 递减连续性（上连续）：条件 $\mu(A_1)<\infty$ 不可省，反例 $A_n=[n,\infty)$。
formulas.noteEn: Continuity from above: the hypothesis $\mu(A_1)<\infty$ is indispensable, with $A_n=[n,\infty)$ as the standard counterexample.

expression.text: (X, ℱ, μ)：X 为非空集合，ℱ 为 σ 代数，μ 为非负可数可加的测度
expression.note: 测度公理：μ(∅)=0 与两两不交集上的可数可加性；概率测度还额外要求 μ(X)=1。
expression.noteEn: The axioms are μ(∅)=0 plus countable additivity on disjoint sets; a probability measure additionally requires μ(X)=1.

properties: 可数可加蕴含有限可加，反之不成立：σ 代数上确实存在只有限可加而不可数可加的集函数。
单调性 $A\subseteq B\Rightarrow\mu(A)\le\mu(B)$；当 $\mu(A)<\infty$ 时还有 $\mu(B\setminus A)=\mu(B)-\mu(A)$。
可数次可加：$\mu(\bigcup_n A_n)\le\sum_n\mu(A_n)$，不需要集列两两不交。
递增连续无条件成立；递减连续需要 $\mu(A_1)<\infty$，否则 $A_n=[n,\infty)$ 给出反例（交集测度为 $0$，极限为 $+\infty$）。
常见实例：计数测度（σ 有限但非有限）、勒贝格测度（σ 有限但非有限）、概率测度（$\mu(X)=1$，有限）。
propertiesEn: Countable additivity implies finite additivity, but not conversely: finitely additive yet not countably additive set functions do exist on σ-algebras.
Monotone: $A\subseteq B$ implies $\mu(A)\le\mu(B)$, and $\mu(B\setminus A)=\mu(B)-\mu(A)$ when $\mu(A)<\infty$.
Countably subadditive: $\mu(\bigcup_n A_n)\le\sum_n\mu(A_n)$, with no disjointness required.

Continuity from below holds unconditionally, while continuity from above needs $\mu(A_1)<\infty$; otherwise $A_n=[n,\infty)$ gives a counterexample (empty intersection of measure 0 versus limit $+\infty$).
Typical examples: counting measure (σ-finite but not finite), Lebesgue measure (σ-finite but not finite) and probability measures ($\mu(X)=1$, finite).

examples.problem: 在 $(\mathbb{R},\mathcal{B},m)$ 中取 $A_n=[n,+\infty)$，验证 $\{A_n\}$ 递减，并说明为什么 $\lim m(A_n)\ne m\bigl(\bigcap_n A_n\bigr)$。
examples.solution: 显然 $A_{n+1}\subseteq A_n$，且 $\bigcap_{n\ge1}A_n=\varnothing$，故 $m(\bigcap_n A_n)=0$。但 $m(A_n)=+\infty$（$[n,+\infty)$ 的外测度为无穷），所以 $\lim_{n}m(A_n)=+\infty$，等式失效。原因正是递减连续性的条件 $m(A_1)<\infty$ 被违反：这里 $m(A_1)=+\infty$。对照递增情形 $B_n=[0,n]$：$m(B_n)=n\to+\infty=m(\bigcup_n B_n)$，无条件成立。

examples.problem: 设 $\mu$ 是 σ 代数 $\mathcal{F}$ 上的集函数，$\mu(\varnothing)=0$，有限可加（两两不交的有限并列可加），且对递增列连续：$A_n\uparrow A\Rightarrow\mu(A_n)\to\mu(A)$。证明 $\mu$ 可数可加。
examples.solution: 设 $\{A_n\}$ 两两不交，令 $S_N=\bigcup_{n\le N}A_n$，则 $S_N\uparrow A=\bigcup_{n\ge1}A_n$。由有限可加性，$\mu(S_N)=\sum_{n=1}^{N}\mu(A_n)$。令 $N\to\infty$ 并用递增连续性： $$\mu(A)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\mu(S_N)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\mu(A_n)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\mu(A_n).$$ 故可数可加成立，且过程中不需要任何有限性假设。这说明「$\mu(\varnothing)=0$ + 有限可加 + 递增连续」是测度公理的等价形式。

title: 可测函数
summary: 可测函数指使每个水平集 {f>a} 可测的函数；它对四则运算与逐点极限封闭，是勒贝格积分的基本对象。
summaryEn: A measurable function is one whose level sets {f>a} are measurable for every real a; the class is closed under arithmetic and pointwise limits, and is the basic object of the Lebesgue integral.
definition:
设 $(X,\mathcal{F})$ 与 $(Y,\mathcal{G})$ 是可测空间。函数 $f:X\to Y$ 称为**可测的**，如果对每个 $B\in\mathcal{G}$ 都有 $$f^{-1}(B)\in\mathcal{F}.$$ 当值域取实数轴 $\mathbb{R}$（配 Borel σ 代数）时，由于 Borel 集由射线 $(a,\infty)$ 生成，判定可测只需检查水平集：$f$ 可测 $\iff$ 对**任意实数 $a$**，$\{x:f(x)>a\}\in\mathcal{F}$。也可以等价地换成 $\ge$、$<$、$\le$ 中的任意一种，因为不同水平集之间只差可数次集合运算，例如 $\{f\ge a\}=\bigcap_{n\ge1}\{f>a-\frac1n\}$。等价地，用「区间」条件 $\{a<f<b\}$（对一切 $a<b$）也是**同样有效**的判据：实值函数下 $\{f>a\}=\bigcup_{n\ge1}\{a<f<a+n\}$，两者可互相推出。只有当函数允许取 $\pm\infty$ 值时区间条件才不足——那时还须额外要求 $\{f=+\infty\}$、$\{f=-\infty\}$ 可测。

与连续函数的关系：连续函数可测（只要 σ 代数相容，如 Borel σ 代数：连续函数把开集的原像拉回开集）。反过来不成立，而且差得很远。**狄利克雷函数** $D(x)=1$（$x\in\mathbb{Q}$）、$D(x)=0$（$x\notin\mathbb{Q}$）处处不连续，却是可测的：对每个 $a$，$\{D>a\}$ 只能是 $\varnothing$、$\mathbb{Q}$ 或 $\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$ 或 $\mathbb{R}$，都是可测集。它甚至不是黎曼可积的，但由于 $\mathbb{Q}$ 是零测集，它在 $[0,1]$ 上的勒贝格积分等于 $0$——这是勒贝格理论威力的第一个预告。

可测函数构成一个向量空间：若 $f,g$ 可测，则 $f+g$、$f-g$、$cf$、$fg$、$\max(f,g)$、$|f|$ 都可测；商 $f/g$ 也可测，只要**分母 $g$ 几乎处处不为零**（$\{g=0\}$ 是零测集），此时在 $g=0$ 处按任意约定（如取 $0$）补定义不影响可测性。更强的是：可测函数列的可数上确界、下确界、上极限、下极限以及逐点极限仍可测。这种对极限运算的封闭性使可测函数类比连续函数类好用得多。

引入可测函数的动机是积分：勒贝格积分先对简单函数定义，再对任意非负可测函数用单调递增的简单函数列的积分取极限——这正是下一节的主题。
definitionEn:
Let $(X,\mathcal{F})$ and $(Y,\mathcal{G})$ be measurable spaces. A function $f:X\to Y$ is **measurable** if $$f^{-1}(B)\in\mathcal{F}\qquad\text{for every }B\in\mathcal{G}.$$ For real-valued functions (with the Borel σ-algebra on $\mathbb{R}$), since Borel sets are generated by the rays $(a,\infty)$, measurability reduces to checking level sets: $f$ is measurable if and only if $\{x:f(x)>a\}\in\mathcal{F}$ for **every real $a$**. One may equivalently use $\ge$, $<$ or $\le$, because the various level sets differ only by countably many set operations, e.g. $\{f\ge a\}=\bigcap_{n\ge1}\{f>a-\frac1n\}$. Equivalently the interval form $\{a<f<b\}$ for all $a<b$ is an equally valid criterion: for a real-valued $f$, $\{f>a\}=\bigcup_{n\ge1}\{a<f<a+n\}$, so the two conditions imply each other. Only when $f$ may take the values $\pm\infty$ does the interval condition fall short, and then $\{f=+\infty\}$, $\{f=-\infty\}$ must be required separately.

As for continuity: a continuous function is measurable whenever the σ-algebras are compatible (as with the Borel σ-algebra, since preimages of open sets are open). The converse fails badly. The **Dirichlet function** $D=1$ on $\mathbb{Q}$ and $D=0$ off $\mathbb{Q}$ is nowhere continuous, yet measurable: for every $a$ the set $\{D>a\}$ is one of $\varnothing,\mathbb{Q},\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q},\mathbb{R}$, all measurable. It is not Riemann integrable, but as $\mathbb{Q}$ is null its Lebesgue integral over $[0,1]$ equals $0$ — a first glimpse of the power of Lebesgue's theory.

Measurable functions form a vector space: if $f,g$ are measurable, so are $f+g$, $f-g$, $cf$, $fg$, $\max(f,g)$ and $|f|$; the quotient $f/g$ is measurable provided the denominator $g$ is nonzero almost everywhere (the null set $\{g=0\}$ may be defined arbitrarily, say as $0$). Even better, countable suprema, infima, limits superior and inferior, and pointwise limits of measurable functions are measurable. This closure under limiting operations makes the class far more useful than continuous functions.

The notion is motivated by integration: the Lebesgue integral is first defined for simple functions, then extended to nonnegative measurable functions as the limit of integrals of increasing simple approximations — the subject of the next section.

formulas.note: 可测函数的一般定义：可测集的原像仍可测。
formulas.noteEn: General definition: the preimage of every measurable set is measurable.

formulas.note: 实值函数的等价判据：水平集 $\{f>a\}$ 可测；也可换成 $\{f\ge a\}$、$\{f<a\}$、$\{f\le a\}$，但要统一使用其中一种。
formulas.noteEn: Equivalent criterion for real-valued functions: the level sets $\{f>a\}$ are measurable; one may replace them by $\{f\ge a\}$, $\{f<a\}$ or $\{f\le a\}$, but must use one fixed form.

formulas.note: 不同水平集之间的转换：说明 $>$ 与 $\ge$ 的判据互相等价。
formulas.noteEn: Conversion between level sets, showing that the '$>$' and '$\ge$' criteria are equivalent.

formulas.note: 对四则运算封闭；除法 $f/g$ 要求分母几乎处处不为零。
formulas.noteEn: Closure under arithmetic; the quotient $f/g$ requires the denominator to be nonzero almost everywhere.

formulas.note: 对可数极限运算封闭：这使可测函数与积分理论紧密配合。
formulas.noteEn: Closure under countable limiting operations, which makes measurable functions mesh with integration theory.

expression.text: f 可测 ⟺ 对每个实数 a，{x : f(x) > a} 可测（换成 ≥、<、≤ 同样等价）
expression.note: 等价定义可固定一种形式的水平集，如 {f > a}；对实值函数，区间形式 {a < f < b} 也是等价的判据。
expression.noteEn: The equivalent definitions may fix one form of level set, e.g. {f > a}; for real-valued functions the interval form {a < f < b} is an equally valid criterion.

properties: 连续函数（在相应 σ 代数下）可测；可测函数可以很不连续，甚至处处不连续（狄利克雷函数）。
可测函数对加、减、乘、数乘、绝对值、取最大/最小封闭；除法 $f/g$ 可测要求分母 $g$ 几乎处处不为零，在 $g=0$ 处任意补定义即可。
可测函数列的可数上确界、下确界、上极限、下极限与逐点极限仍可测。
若 $g$ 连续（更一般地 $g$ 为 Borel 可测），则 $g\circ f$ 可测；若 $g$ 只是勒贝格可测，复合可能失去可测性。
两个可测函数之集 $\{f>g\}$、$\{f=g\}$ 与 $\{f=c\}$ 都可测。
propertiesEn: Continuous functions (for compatible σ-algebras) are measurable; measurable functions may be nowhere continuous, as the Dirichlet function shows.

Measurable functions are closed under sums, differences, products, scalar multiples, $|f|$ and max/min; the quotient $f/g$ is measurable provided $g\ne0$ almost everywhere, with arbitrary values where $g=0$.
Countable suprema, infima, limits superior and inferior, and pointwise limits of measurable functions are measurable.
If $g$ is continuous (more generally Borel measurable) then $g\circ f$ is measurable; if $g$ is merely Lebesgue measurable the composition can fail to be measurable.
For measurable $f$ and $g$, the sets $\{f>g\}$, $\{f=g\}$ and $\{f=c\}$ are all measurable.

examples.problem: 验证狄利克雷函数 $D(x)=1$（$x\in\mathbb{Q}$）、$D(x)=0$（$x\notin\mathbb{Q}$）是可测函数，并说明它处处不连续。
examples.solution: 对任意 $a\in\mathbb{R}$ 分情况讨论 $\{D>a\}$：若 $a<0$，该集合为 $\mathbb{R}$；若 $0\le a<1$，该集合为 $\mathbb{Q}$；若 $a\ge1$，该集合为 $\varnothing$。三者都是 Borel 集，故 $D$ 可测。处处不连续：任取 $x_0$，取有理数列 $q_n\to x_0$ 与无理数列 $r_n\to x_0$，则 $D(q_n)=1\to1$ 而 $D(r_n)=0\to0$，极限不唯一，故 $D$ 在 $x_0$ 不连续。又 $\mathbb{Q}$ 是零测集，所以 $D=0$ 几乎处处成立，它在 $[0,1]$ 上的勒贝格积分为 $0$，尽管它不是黎曼可积的。

examples.problem: 证明：$f$ 可测 $\Rightarrow$ $|f|$ 可测；并说明反过来不成立。
examples.solution: 对任意 $a\ge0$，$\{|f|>a\}=\{f>a\}\cup\{f<-a\}$ 是两个可测集之并，可测；当 $a<0$ 时 $\{|f|>a\}=\mathbb{R}$，可测。所以 $|f|$ 可测。反过来：取不可测集 $A$（维塔利集，其存在性是勒贝格测度理论的经典事实），令 $$f=1_{A}-1_{A^{c}}=\begin{cases}1,&x\in A,\\ -1,&x\notin A.\end{cases}$$ 则 $|f|\equiv1$ 可测，但 $\{f>0\}=A$ 不可测，故 $f$ 不可测。这说明「取绝对值」会丢失符号信息，可测性不能从 $|f|$ 反推 $f$。

title: 简单函数与可测函数的逼近
titleEn: Simple Functions and Approximation of Measurable Functions
summary: 简单函数是有限个可测集示性函数的线性组合；每个非负可测函数都是某个单调递增简单函数列的逐点极限，这是勒贝格积分的起点。
summaryEn: Simple functions are finite linear combinations of indicators of measurable sets; every nonnegative measurable function is the pointwise limit of an increasing sequence of simple functions, the starting point of the Lebesgue integral.
definition:
**简单函数**是指取有限个值的可测函数，等价地可以写成 $$\varphi=\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_i\chi_{E_i},$$ 其中 $c_i$ 是常数，$E_i$ 是可测集且两两不交，$\chi_{E_i}$ 是**示性函数**（$x\in E_i$ 时取 $1$，否则取 $0$）。示性函数本身是最简单的简单函数；有限线性组合、有限个简单函数的和与积仍是简单函数。

为什么盯住简单函数？因为它们太容易积分了：对非负简单函数 $\varphi=\sum c_i\chi_{E_i}$，勒贝格积分就直接定义为 $$\int_X\varphi\,d\mu=\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_i\,\mu(E_i),$$ 完全不需要像黎曼积分那样分割定义域再取极限。于是问题只剩下一个：一般可测函数能不能用简单函数「逼近」出来？答案是能，而且逼近得非常强。

**【关键定理】** 设 $f\ge0$ 可测。则存在简单函数列 $\{\varphi_n\}$，满足 (i) $0\le\varphi_1\le\varphi_2\le\cdots\le f$（**单调递增**）；(ii) 对每个 $x$，$\varphi_n(x)\to f(x)$（逐点收敛）。标准构造是把值域 $[0,n]$ 等分成 $n2^n$ 段、并允许超过 $n$ 时取 $n$：$$\varphi_n=\sum_{k=1}^{n2^n}\frac{k-1}{2^n}\,\chi_{\{\frac{k-1}{2^n}\le f<\frac{k}{2^n}\}}+n\,\chi_{\{f\ge n\}}.$$ 随着 $n$ 增大，网格变细、截断值 $n$ 升高，两个来源的误差都趋于零，且可以验证 $\varphi_n\le\varphi_{n+1}\le f$。

对一般的（可正可负的）可测函数 $f$，把它拆成正部与负部 $f=f^{+}-f^{-}$ 分别逼近再相减即可；此时单调性一般不保持，但有 $|\varphi_n|\le|f|$ 且 $\varphi_n\to f$ 逐点。定理说明：简单函数在逐点逼近的意义下「稠密」于可测函数空间，因此许多积分定理（如单调收敛定理）只需先对简单函数证明，再用逼近过渡到一般可测函数。
definitionEn:
A **simple function** is a measurable function taking finitely many values; equivalently, $$\varphi=\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_i\chi_{E_i},$$ where the $c_i$ are constants, the measurable sets $E_i$ are pairwise disjoint, and $\chi_{E_i}$ is the **indicator** of $E_i$ (equal to $1$ on $E_i$ and $0$ outside). Indicators are the simplest examples, and finite linear combinations, sums and products of simple functions remain simple.

Why simple functions? Because they are trivially integrable: for a nonnegative simple function $\varphi=\sum c_i\chi_{E_i}$ the Lebesgue integral is defined directly by $$\int_X\varphi\,d\mu=\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_i\,\mu(E_i),$$ with no partition-of-the-domain limit as in Riemann's theory. The only remaining question is whether simple functions can approximate a general measurable function — and the answer is a strong yes.

**Key theorem.** If $f\ge0$ is measurable, there exist simple functions $\varphi_n$ with (i) $0\le\varphi_1\le\varphi_2\le\cdots\le f$ (**monotone**); (ii) $\varphi_n(x)\to f(x)$ for every $x$ (pointwise). The standard construction splits the range on $[0,n]$ into $n2^n$ equal pieces and truncates above $n$: $$\varphi_n=\sum_{k=1}^{n2^n}\frac{k-1}{2^n}\,\chi_{\{\frac{k-1}{2^n}\le f<\frac{k}{2^n}\}}+n\,\chi_{\{f\ge n\}}.$$ As $n$ grows the grid gets finer and the truncation level rises, so both error sources vanish and one checks that $\varphi_n\le\varphi_{n+1}\le f$.

For a general (signed) measurable $f$ one writes $f=f^{+}-f^{-}$, approximates both parts and subtracts; monotonicity is then usually lost, but one still has $|\varphi_n|\le|f|$ and $\varphi_n\to f$ pointwise. Hence simple functions are pointwise dense in the space of measurable functions, and many integral theorems (monotone convergence, for instance) are first proved for simple functions and then extended by approximation.

formulas.note: 简单函数的一般形式：有限个可测集示性函数的线性组合。
formulas.noteEn: General form of a simple function: a finite linear combination of indicators of measurable sets.

formulas.note: 简单函数的积分定义（对非负简单函数）：只依赖各水平集的测度。
formulas.noteEn: Integral of a nonnegative simple function: it depends only on the measures of the level sets.

formulas.note: 标准逼近构造：把 $[0,n]$ 等分并截断，$\varphi_n$ 单调递增地逼近 $f$。
formulas.noteEn: The standard approximation: partition $[0,n]$ and truncate, so that $\varphi_n$ increases to $f$.

formulas.note: 逼近定理的两条结论：单调递增且逐点收敛。
formulas.noteEn: The two conclusions of the approximation theorem: monotone increase and pointwise convergence.

formulas.note: 非负可测函数的积分定义：所有不超过 $f$ 的非负简单函数之积分的上确界。
formulas.noteEn: Definition of the integral for nonnegative measurable functions: the supremum of the integrals of nonnegative simple functions dominated by $f$.

expression.text: φ = Σᵢ cᵢ·χ_{Eᵢ}（Eᵢ 两两不交、可测，cᵢ 为常数）
expression.note: 示性函数 χ_E 在 E 上取 1、在 E 外取 0；取有限个值的函数是简单函数当且仅当每个水平集可测。
expression.noteEn: The indicator χ_E is 1 on E and 0 outside; a function with finitely many values is simple exactly when all its level sets are measurable.

properties: 取有限个值的可测函数恰是简单函数；示性函数是特殊的简单函数，阶梯函数是典型例子。
简单函数对线性组合、和、差、积封闭，运算结果仍取有限个值。
非负简单函数的积分 $\int\varphi\,d\mu=\sum_i c_i\mu(E_i)$ 具有线性与单调性，不同分解方式给出同一个值。
对非负可测函数 $f$，存在简单函数列满足 $0\le\varphi_1\le\varphi_2\le\cdots\le f$ 且 $\varphi_n(x)\to f(x)$；对一般可测函数可拆成 $f=f^{+}-f^{-}$，用 $|\varphi_n|\le|f|$ 的简单函数列逼近。
逼近定理把积分问题化归为简单函数：非负可测函数的积分定义为所有不超过它的非负简单函数之积分的上确界，单调收敛定理由此展开。
propertiesEn: A measurable function with finitely many values is exactly a simple function; indicators are special cases and step functions are the typical picture.
Simple functions are closed under linear combinations, sums, differences and products, and the results still take finitely many values.
For nonnegative simple functions, $\int\varphi\,d\mu=\sum_i c_i\mu(E_i)$ is linear and monotone, and different disjoint decompositions give the same value.

For nonnegative measurable $f$ there are simple $\varphi_n$ with $0\le\varphi_1\le\varphi_2\le\cdots\le f$ and $\varphi_n\to f$ pointwise; a general measurable $f$ is handled through $f=f^{+}-f^{-}$ with $|\varphi_n|\le|f|$.

The theorem reduces integration to simple functions: the integral of a nonnegative measurable function is the supremum of the integrals of the nonnegative simple functions dominated by it, on which the monotone convergence theorem is built.

examples.problem: 验证 $s_n(x)=\bigl(\lfloor 2^n x\rfloor/2^n\bigr)^2$ 在 $[0,2]$ 上是简单函数，并说明 $\{s_n\}$ 单调递增且逐点收敛到 $f(x)=x^2$。
examples.solution: 对每个 $n$，$s_n$ 在每个小区间 $\bigl[\frac{k}{2^n},\frac{k+1}{2^n}\bigr)$ 上取常值 $\bigl(\frac{k}{2^n}\bigr)^2$（$k=0,1,\dots,2^{n+1}-1$），只取有限个值且各水平集是区间（可测），故为简单函数。单调性：记 $k_n=\lfloor2^n x\rfloor$，网格加密时 $k_{n+1}/2^{n+1}\ge k_n/2^n$，故 $s_{n+1}(x)\ge s_n(x)$。收敛：由 $0\le x-k_n/2^n<2^{-n}$ 得 $k_n/2^n\to x$，平方得 $s_n(x)\to x^2$；并且始终有 $s_n(x)\le x^2$。这正是「非负可测函数被单调递增简单函数列逼近」的具体实例。

examples.problem: 设 $E$ 可测，$\varphi=2\chi_{E}+3\chi_{\mathbb{R}\setminus E}$，且已知 $m(E\cap[0,1])=\frac14$。用简单函数的积分公式计算 $\int_{[0,1]}\varphi\,dm$。
examples.solution: $\varphi$ 只取 $2$ 与 $3$ 两个值，是简单函数。在 $[0,1]$ 上按不交可测集分解（注意 $E\cap[0,1]$ 与 $[0,1]\setminus E$ 不交、并为 $[0,1]$）： $$\int_{[0,1]}\varphi\,dm=2\,m(E\cap[0,1])+3\,m([0,1]\setminus E)=2\cdot\frac14+3\cdot\frac34=\frac{11}{4}.$$ 可见简单函数的积分只关心各个水平集的测度，与集合的具体形状无关。

title: 几乎处处收敛与依测度收敛
titleEn: Almost Everywhere and Convergence in Measure
summary: 几乎处处收敛允许在一个零测集上不收敛，依测度收敛则要求偏差超过任意 ε 的集合测度趋于零；二者互不包含，有限测度下前者蕴含后者。
summaryEn: Almost everywhere convergence forgives a null set, while convergence in measure demands that the sets where the deviation exceeds any ε shrink to measure zero; neither implies the other, though a.e. convergence does imply it for finite measures.
definition:
在测度空间中，「函数列收敛」不止一种含义，因为人们愿意原谅测度为 $0$ 的坏点。设 $(X,\mathcal{F},\mu)$ 是测度空间，$f_n,f$ 可测。称 $f_n$ **几乎处处收敛**（a.e. 收敛）于 $f$，如果存在零测集 $N$（$\mu(N)=0$），使得对所有 $x\notin N$ 都有 $f_n(x)\to f(x)$；换言之，不收敛的点集是零测集。例如 $f_n(x)=x^n$ 在 $[0,1]$ 上不处处收敛到 $0$（在 $x=1$ 处 $f_n(1)=1$），但 $\{1\}$ 是零测集，所以它几乎处处收敛到 $0$。

另一种收敛方式是**依测度收敛**：对任何 $\varepsilon>0$，$$\mu\bigl(\{x:|f_n(x)-f(x)|\ge\varepsilon\}\bigr)\to0\qquad(n\to\infty).$$ 它的意思是：偏差大的集合在测度意义下越来越小，并不要求每一点都安定下来。它把「逐点」换成了「测度」。

两种收敛的关系是实变函数里最爱考的反例工厂。**a.e. 收敛一般推不出依测度收敛**：在 $\mathbb{R}$ 上取勒贝格测度与 $f_n=\chi_{[n,n+1)}$，每个点只属于有限多个这样的区间，故 $f_n(x)\to0$ 处处成立，但 $m(\{|f_n-0|\ge\frac12\})=1$ 不趋于 $0$，不依测度收敛。一旦加上**有限测度**条件（$\mu(X)<\infty$），a.e. 收敛就蕴含依测度收敛（叶戈罗夫定理可以给出更漂亮的一致收敛版本）。

反方向：**依测度收敛也推不出 a.e. 收敛**，而且这不需要任何有限性假设的让步——即使测度有限也不成立。经典反例是 $[0,1]$ 上的「滑动区间」：把 $f_{n,k}=\chi_{[k/n,(k+1)/n)}$（$k=0,\dots,n-1$）按 $n$ 递增排成一列，则每个集合的测度为 $1/n\to0$，故依测度收敛到 $0$；但每个 $x\in[0,1)$ 在每一层 $n$ 都被某个区间盖住，于是无穷多次取到 $1$，极限不存在，故不 a.e. 收敛。不过**依测度收敛的序列总能取出一个 a.e. 收敛的子列**（取子列使 $\mu(\{|f_{n_j}-f|\ge\frac1j\})\le2^{-j}$，再用 Borel–Cantelli 引理），子列是这道裂缝唯一的补救。
definitionEn:
In a measure space 'convergence of a sequence of functions' has more than one useful meaning, because behaviour on a null set may be forgiven. Let $(X,\mathcal{F},\mu)$ be a measure space and $f_n,f$ measurable. We say $f_n\to f$ **almost everywhere** (a.e.) if there is a null set $N$ with $\mu(N)=0$ such that $f_n(x)\to f(x)$ for every $x\notin N$; the set where convergence fails has measure zero. For instance $f_n(x)=x^n$ on $[0,1]$ does not converge everywhere to $0$ (at $x=1$, $f_n(1)=1$), but $\{1\}$ is null, so it converges a.e. to $0$.

Another notion is **convergence in measure**: for every $\varepsilon>0$, $$\mu\bigl(\{x:|f_n(x)-f(x)|\ge\varepsilon\}\bigr)\to0\qquad(n\to\infty).$$ Large deviations occur on sets that become small; no individual point is required to settle down. The pointwise requirement is replaced by a measure-theoretic one.

The relation between the two is a classical source of counterexamples. **Almost everywhere convergence does not imply convergence in measure** in general: on $\mathbb{R}$ with Lebesgue measure take $f_n=\chi_{[n,n+1)}$. Every point lies in at most one of these intervals, so $f_n\to0$ everywhere, yet $m(\{|f_n|\ge\frac12\})=1$ does not tend to $0$. Once the measure is **finite** ($\mu(X)<\infty$), a.e. convergence does imply convergence in measure (Egorov's theorem gives a sharper, uniform version).

Conversely, **convergence in measure does not imply a.e. convergence**, and this survives even finite measures. The classical counterexample is the sliding-interval sequence on $[0,1]$: enumerate $f_{n,k}=\chi_{[k/n,(k+1)/n)}$ with $k=0,\dots,n-1$ and let $n$ increase. Each set has measure $1/n\to0$, so $f\to0$ in measure; but every $x\in[0,1)$ is hit once at each level $n$, hence infinitely often, so the limit fails to exist almost everywhere. The gap is bridged by subsequences: convergence in measure always yields a subsequence converging a.e. (choose $n_j$ with $\mu(\{|f_{n_j}-f|\ge\frac1j\})\le2^{-j}$ and apply Borel–Cantelli).

formulas.note: 几乎处处收敛：不收敛的点集是零测集，去掉它之后逐点收敛。
formulas.noteEn: Almost everywhere convergence: the set of points where convergence fails is null.

formulas.note: 依测度收敛：偏差超过任意给定 $\varepsilon$ 的集合测度趋于零。
formulas.noteEn: Convergence in measure: the measure of the set where the deviation exceeds any given ε tends to zero.

formulas.note: 有限测度下 a.e. 收敛蕴含依测度收敛（叶戈罗夫定理）；一般测度空间中不成立，反例 $\chi_{[n,n+1)}$。
formulas.noteEn: With finite measure, a.e. convergence implies convergence in measure (Egorov); in general measure spaces this fails, with χ_[n,n+1) as counterexample.

formulas.note: 依测度收敛不能整体升格为 a.e. 收敛，但总能取出 a.e. 收敛的子列。
formulas.noteEn: Convergence in measure cannot be upgraded globally to a.e. convergence, but an a.e. convergent subsequence always exists.

formulas.note: 有限测度空间中，依测度收敛由这个度量给出；a.e. 收敛一般不来自任何度量，二者强弱关系不对称。
formulas.noteEn: On finite measure spaces convergence in measure is induced by this metric; a.e. convergence generally comes from no metric, so the two notions are asymmetric.

expression.text: a.e. 收敛：去掉零测集后逐点收敛；依测度收敛：对每个 ε>0，m({|fₙ−f| ≥ ε}) → 0
expression.note: 符号表示依测度收敛；概率论中称为依概率收敛。有限测度下 a.e. 收敛蕴含依测度收敛，反之只能取出 a.e. 收敛的子列。
expression.noteEn: The symbol denotes convergence in measure, called convergence in probability in probability theory. On finite measure spaces a.e. convergence implies it; conversely only an a.e. convergent subsequence can be extracted.

properties: 有限测度空间中 a.e. 收敛蕴含依测度收敛；一般测度空间不成立，反例 $\chi_{[n,n+1)}$ 在 $\mathbb{R}$ 上处处收敛却不依测度收敛。
依测度收敛蕴含存在子列 a.e. 收敛；但整体不一定 a.e. 收敛，即使测度有限（$[0,1]$ 上的滑动区间反例）。
依测度收敛的极限在 a.e. 意义下唯一：若 $f_n\to f$ 且 $f_n\to g$ 依测度，则 $\mu(\{f\ne g\})=0$。
概率论中 $P(\Omega)=1<\infty$，故几乎必然收敛蕴含依概率收敛；依概率收敛不蕴含几乎必然收敛。
有限测度下叶戈罗夫定理更强：a.e. 收敛的序列去掉任意小测度集后一致收敛（见叶戈罗夫与卢津定理）。
propertiesEn: On finite measure spaces a.e. convergence implies convergence in measure; in general it does not, as χ_[n,n+1) on ℝ converges everywhere but not in measure.
Convergence in measure yields an a.e. convergent subsequence, yet need not itself be a.e. convergent, even for finite measures (sliding intervals on [0,1]).
Limits in measure are a.e. unique: if f_n→f and f_n→g in measure then μ({f≠g})=0.
In probability theory P(Ω)=1<∞, so almost sure convergence implies convergence in probability, but not conversely.
For finite measures Egorov's theorem is stronger: an a.e. convergent sequence becomes uniformly convergent after removing sets of arbitrarily small measure (see the Egorov–Lusin node).

examples.problem: 在 $(\mathbb{R},\mathcal{B},m)$ 上取 $f_n=\chi_{[n,n+1)}$，判断 $f_n$ 是否几乎处处收敛到 $0$、是否依测度收敛到 $0$。
examples.solution: a.e. 收敛：对每个实数 $x$，只有唯一的整数 $n_0=\lfloor x\rfloor$ 满足 $x\in[n_0,n_0+1)$，故当 $n\ne n_0$ 时 $f_n(x)=0$，于是 $f_n(x)\to0$ 对一切 $x$ 成立，当然也 a.e. 收敛。依测度收敛：对 $0<\varepsilon\le1$，$\{x:|f_n(x)-0|\ge\varepsilon\}=[n,n+1)$，其测度恒为 $1$，不趋于 $0$，故不依测度收敛。这说明在一般的（非有限）测度空间中，a.e. 收敛推不出依测度收敛。

examples.problem: 在 $[0,1]$ 上按 $n=1,2,3,\dots$、每个 $n$ 取 $k=0,1,\dots,n-1$ 的顺序排列滑动区间 $f_{n,k}=\chi_{[k/n,(k+1)/n)}$。证明它依测度收敛到 $0$，但不几乎处处收敛；并指出如何取出 a.e. 收敛的子列。
examples.solution: 依测度收敛：任取 $\varepsilon>0$（不妨 $\varepsilon\le1$），$\{f_{n,k}\ge\varepsilon\}=[k/n,(k+1)/n)$，测度为 $1/n$；当序号趋于无穷时 $n\to\infty$，故测度趋于 $0$。不 a.e. 收敛：任取 $x\in[0,1)$ 与任取 $n$，存在唯一的 $k$ 使 $x\in[k/n,(k+1)/n)$，于是 $f_{n,k}(x)=1$；由于 $n$ 取遍所有正整数，该列在 $x$ 处无穷多次取 $1$（也无穷多次取 $0$），极限不存在。不收敛的点构成 $[0,1)$，测度为 $1>0$，故不 a.e. 收敛。取出子列：只保留 $k=0$ 的那一部分，即 $\chi_{[0,1/n)}$，它对每个 $x\in(0,1]$ 最终为 $0$，仅在 $x=0$ 处始终取 $1$，而 $\{0\}$ 是零测集，故该子列 a.e. 收敛到 $0$——这印证了「依测度收敛总可取出 a.e. 收敛的子列」。
